Acute or chronic disseminated in- fection involving widespread infiltration of the reticuloen- dothelial system, is mainly seen in immunodeficient or im- munocompromised patients. Histoplasma capsulatum var. duboisii is found in Africa and may cause a chronic disseminated form of histoplas- mosis with focal lesions predominantly in skin and bone. Antifungal therapy for histoplasmosis is necessary in pa- tients with severe acute pulmonary infections, chronic pul- 520 Antifungals monary disease, or disseminated infection. Infections which are not life-threatening but not resolving spontane- ously may be treated with an oral azole in both immuno- competent and immunocompromised patients.1,2 Itracona- zole is the preferred drug.1,2 Ketoconazole is moderately effective but more toxic. Fluconazole is less effective than either itraconazole or ketoconazole.2-4 Patients with chron- ic cavitary pulmonary histoplasmosis should be treated with oral itraconazole for a minimum of 1 year.1 Patients with moderately severe to severe acute pulmonary histo- plasmosis may be treated with intravenous liposomal am- photericin B for 1 to 2 weeks followed by oral itraconazole for a total of 12 weeks. Conventional intravenous ampho- tericin B may be given as an alternative. The same treat- ment regimen is recommended for those with progressive disseminated disease; oral itraconazole in these patients should be continued for 12 months.1 Immunocompro- mised patients, including those with HIV infection, may need to continue maintenance therapy indefinitely, with itraconazole daily or amphotericin B weekly,1-3,5 if immu- nosuppression cannot be reversed.1 Patients with CNS his- toplasmosis should be given intravenous liposomal am- photericin B for 4 to 6 weeks, followed by oral itraconazole for a minimum of 1 year.1 Primary prophylax- is with itraconazole is not recommended routinely but may be considered for patients with advanced AIDS at espe- cially high risk of infection due to occupational exposure or residence in a hyperendemic area.5 1.
